key_insight: A physics-informed neural network with exact boundary and initial constraints identifies the shear piezoelectric coefficient e15 from sparse, noisy simulated wavefields with low error.
engineering_relevance: The approach could enable non-destructive characterization of shear coupling for PMUT and surface acoustic wave devices, reducing reliance on destructive resonance tests.
method: Embed spatial distance functions and temporal multipliers into network outputs to enforce boundary and initial conditions exactly.
Train on coupled electro-elastodynamic equations and sparse observations without boundary or initial-condition penalty weights.
Non-dimensionalize governing coefficients to improve numerical conditioning.
evidence_signal: On finite-element data from one subsurface line, the full formulation achieved 1.19% mean e15 error at 30 dB noise and 0.65–2.71% across a 40–0 dB sweep; displacement-only training also recovered e15.
watch_item: Validation is simulation-based; performance on experimental measurements and sensitivity to model or boundary-condition mismatch remain unestablished.
paper_title: Identifying the Shear Piezoelectric Coefficient using Physics-Informed Neural Networks under Exact Boundary and Initial Constraints
